spec.name: rotl-mix-xor-v1
spec.limitations: Per-byte only: no diffusion across byte positions, so equal plaintext bytes produce equal ciphertext bytes at every offset (ECB-style pattern leakage). Effective key entropy is 8 bits: one known plaintext/ciphertext byte pair reduces the key to a brute-force scan of 256 candidates, and the fixed constants (23, 165, 90) and rotations (3, 5) add no secret entropy. It is a keyed byte permutation, not a cipher, and is expected to fail immediately under known-plaintext or repeated-structure analysis. Only xor_key is used so the inverse stays inside the same op set; an add_key step would push a modular subtraction of the secret into the inverse, which the op set cannot express.
spec.math: With k the secret byte: x1 = x xor k, x2 = rol3(x1), x3 = x2 + 23 (mod 256), x4 = x3 xor 165, x5 = x4 xor k, x6 = rol5(x5), y = x6 + 90 (mod 256). Every step is a bijection on the 256-byte set: xor with a constant is an involution, addition mod 256 is a permutation whose inverse is addition of 256-c, and rol n permutes the 8 bit positions with inverse rol((8-n) mod 8), so rol3 and rol5 are mutually inverse. A composition of bijections is a bijection, hence exactly invertible for every k. Inversion runs the reversed ops with reversed arguments: y -> add 166 (= -90) -> rol 3 -> xor k -> xor 165 -> add 233 (= -23) -> rol 5 -> xor k, recovering x.
spec.assumptions: The key k is a fixed secret byte chosen uniformly and reused for every input byte; operations apply independently per byte with rol wrapping inside 8 bits (n reduced mod 8); all other operands are constants known to both sides; no nonce, IV, or chaining is assumed; the environment accepts *_key operands that are ignored.
